Learn the game in five minutes

Kalmia Mission Control turns Class 15 into missions: you rebuild each idea from its basic truths, then use it. This page shows every screen with a short animation recorded from the real game, so you can play efficiently from the first minute.

Then use “Slides + notes” and “Lecture” whenever you need the full explanation — tonight for Lab 4, Part F, and before Monday's Quiz 4.

1Start in three steps⏱ 1 min

  1. Download 420-1C2-DW_Class15_Game_KalmiaMissionControl.html and open it in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Nothing to install; it works without Internet (only the videos and links need it).
  2. On the map, follow the dashed path from Launch to Debrief — or click any station or menu button to jump there.
  3. Watch the top right: your XP (experience points), your level (Intern → Risk lead) and your badges. They are saved in this browser only.
Tip: The menu bar is always visible: “Map” brings you back home from anywhere.

2How every mission works: first principles⏱ 30 s

  1. Boil it down — read the three basic truths of the mission (left card).
  2. Ask “why?” — click the rust button three times; each click reveals the next reason (+10 XP [experience points] for the three).
  3. Build it up — do the challenges below: each one turns a truth into an action. “See the slide” opens the matching slide.
Tip: Say each “why” answer aloud before clicking again: it is the fastest way to remember it.

3Launch — rebuild the one fact⏱ 2 min

  1. Click the sentence pieces in the right order; a wrong piece flashes red and nothing is lost.
  2. When the sentence is complete you get the three words — right people · trusted numbers · justified order — and your first badge.
Tip: These three words are the plan of the whole class: Mission 1, 2 and 3.

4Mission 1 — Right people⏱ 6 min

  1. Who receives what? Click a document, then click the reader who needs it. Press Check: green slots are right.
  2. Nadia Roy's page — click the six contents in order. BLUF (bottom line up front): the decisions come first.
  3. The finding for R-01 — click a sentence, then criteria, condition, cause or effect. Check.
Tip: Ask what each reader decides or does: the level of detail follows the task, not the rank.

5Mission 2 — Trusted numbers⏱ 6 min

  1. Ethics gate — choose the professional answer to four requests; every option explains itself.
  2. Redaction hunt — click every item that must not reach the management copy (IP [Internet Protocol] addresses, account names, CVE [Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures] numbers, personal e-mail and phone). Then press “Run the verification”.
  3. Label what leaves — pick a Kalmia level or a TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) label for five documents, then Check.
Tip: Watch the capitals: one account name hides in upper case — exactly the trap of Code example 2.

6Mission 3 — Justified order⏱ 7 min

  1. Six questions — click them in their order: must · class · first four · value · dependency · capacity-calendar-budget.
  2. Deadlines — read exposed · KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities) · automatable · impact and choose the BOD (Binding Operational Directive) 26-04 timeline.
  3. Cut line — click the first action that no longer fits in $20,000, then the cheaper one further down that still fits.
  4. Order four actions — click CT-36, CT-09, CT-24 and CT-21 in the order you would start them.
Tip: Use the “Running total if funded” column: the cut line is where it passes $20,000.

7Flash-card arcade⏱ 4 min

  1. Click the card to turn it. Answer aloud first.
  2. Be honest: “I knew it ✓” removes the card (+10 XP [experience points]); “Not yet” keeps it in the deck for later.
  3. The ring counts the cards you know; all 25 give the “Card shark” badge.
Tip: Two short rounds work better than one long one.

8Quiz boss⏱ 8 min

  1. The 18 formative questions of the lecture. One answer: click it. Several answers: select them all, then “Attack!”.
  2. A hint costs 5 XP (experience points); every option shows why it is right or wrong after you answer.
  3. 14 hits defeat the boss. Missed? Press “Fight again”: the questions come in a new order.
Tip: Formative only: Quiz 4 on Monday is a separate assessment.

9Word match — abbreviations⏱ 2 min

  1. Turn two cards. An abbreviation and its full name form a pair and stay open.
  2. Six pairs per deal; “New deal” gives six others from the abbreviations of the class.
Tip: Say the full name before you turn the second card.

10Slides with the full notes, and the lecture⏱ any

  1. “Slides + notes”: click a thumbnail or use Prev / Next (or ← →). The right column is the professor's script for that slide.
  2. “In the lecture” chips open the matching part of the lecture text; in the lecture, the slide chips open the slide again.
  3. “Projector” opens the slide in a separate window for a second screen.
Tip: Before Lab 4, read the slides of Lesson 3 with their notes: they contain the Part F decisions.

11Debrief — your badges⏱ 1 min

  1. See your XP (experience points), your level and the ten badges; grey badges are still to win.
  2. The debrief also lists tonight's workshop (Hours 2 to 4) and the Lab 4 due date.
  3. “Reset my progress” erases your progress in this browser (click twice to confirm).
Tip: Using another computer or a private window? Your progress does not follow you: it stays in the browser where you played.

Questions and problems

Does the game need the Internet?

No. Everything is inside the file. Only the videos and the official links open web pages.

My progress disappeared.

Progress is kept by the browser on this computer. A private window, another browser or another computer starts from zero.

The projector window does not open.

Your browser blocked the pop-up window: allow pop-ups for this file, then click “Projector” again.

A mission does not turn gold on the map.

Every challenge of the mission must be completed: look for the green “✓” messages under each stage.

Is this Quiz 4?

No. The game, its quiz and its flash-cards are formative practice. Quiz 4 (Monday, November 23) is separate.
